summary: Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1807), the University of Göttingen (1809), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811). He held a post at the University of Berlin (Humboldt University of Berlin) from circa 1820 to 1831.

Arthur W. Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1894–1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and at Leipzig University (~1901–1902) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (~1902–1906) and was a professor at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).

Arthur Waley worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rugby School and King's College, and having studied under Gustav Haloun, he held posts at the British Museum (1913) and SOAS University of London (~1934–1939).
Aruna Haldar is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedar Nath Ojha. She worked as a teacher at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who studied under M. V. Upadhyay and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (~1948–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Baroda College (~1946–1957).

Arvind Sharma is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. He held positions at Queensland, Harvard (Infinity Foundation Visiting Professor), and McGill (Birks Chair, circa 1987).

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Head of Buddhist thought (attested 1993), Professor (~1996–2009), and Head of Buddhist Philosophy (~2003–2009).
Asatoshi Kamiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University and worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).
Asef Bayat studied at the University of Kent (~1979–1984). He held academic posts at Leiden University (2000–2010) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2010).
Asen Balikci studied at Columbia University (~1957–1962) and held a post at the Université de Montréal from circa 1968 to 1994.

Ashby Butnor is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Hawaii under Vrinda Dalmiya in 2009. She was a Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver (attested 2011).

Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), he served as a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1969–2006).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1968) and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.
Ashok Vajpeyi is an Indologist who completed an MA while studying at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, circa 1961–1963.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a historian and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (~1963–1967), where he later was a Senior Research Fellow (~1968–1972). He also lectured in English at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, the Academy of Finland, and the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Asutosh Mookerjee worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he later held posts (1906–1914) and served as President (1921–1923). He was also at Calcutta High Court (1904).

Atsuhiko Yoshida is a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Seikei University (~1951–1955) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1960), and later held a post at Seikei University (~1974–1999).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as a lecturer at Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989) and as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (attested 1996–2003, 2012).
